summary: This article explains how most of Earth's volcanoes erupt hidden under the ocean, building new seafloor, seamounts and islands, feeding strange life at hot vents, and slowly widening the Red Sea.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Volcanoes Under the Sea” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: a mountain under the sea that was made by a volcano
a long, narrow line of high land or mountains
the force of something pressing or pushing on something else

challengeTerms.def: having to do with the huge moving pieces of the Earth's outer layer
having to do with water that has been heated deep inside the Earth
a small vessel built to travel deep under the water

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that exploring the deep sea is just as important as exploring space? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how an underwater volcano can become an island.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review seamount, ridge, and pressure, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tectonic, hydrothermal, and submersible to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
